_comment: Syntax of the Mermaid diagram types the AI prompts teach, verified against the bundled mermaid (frontend/src/utils/__tests__/mermaidReference.test.ts parses every example and checks every invalid sample fails). Update together with the frontend's mermaid.

types.use_for: brainstorm / idea map around one central topic
rules: Exactly one root; all other nodes nest under it by indentation.
Shapes: id[square], id(rounded), id((circle)), id{{hexagon}}, id))bang((, id)cloud(.
Text with parentheses or brackets goes quoted after an id: ads["Ads (paid)"], never a bare "quoted line". Don't use front matter `layout: elk`.
types.example:
mindmap
  root((Product launch))
    Marketing
      Blog post
      ads["Social ads (paid)"]
    Engineering
      qa{{Load testing}}
    Support
      help(Help center)

types.use_for: chronological events or milestones by period
rules: Lines are `period : event`; add events with more ` : event` or a next line starting with `:`.
`section Name` groups the following periods; no colon inside section names.
types.example:
timeline
  title Product history
  section Early days
    2019 : Prototype
    2020 : First customers : Seed round
  section Growth
    2022 : Team of 50
         : Berlin office

types.use_for: 2x2 matrix rating items on two criteria (effort vs impact)
rules: Points `Name: [x, y]` with x and y from 0 to 1 (no percentages or negatives).
`x-axis Low --> High`; quadrant-1 is top-right, 2 top-left, 3 bottom-left, 4 bottom-right.
Quote names with punctuation: "SSO (beta)": [0.7, 0.8].
types.example:
quadrantChart
  title Feature prioritization
  x-axis Low effort --> High effort
  y-axis Low impact --> High impact
  quadrant-1 Plan carefully
  quadrant-2 Quick wins
  quadrant-3 Fill-ins
  quadrant-4 Avoid
  Dark mode: [0.25, 0.80]
  "SSO (beta)": [0.75, 0.85]
invalid:
quadrantChart
  x-axis Low --> High
  y-axis Low --> High
  Item A: [30, 60]

types.use_for: user journey steps scored by satisfaction
rules: Tasks are `Task name: score: Actor1, Actor2` (colons, score 1 bad to 5 good) under `section Name`.
types.example:
journey
  title Buying a laptop online
  section Research
    Compare models: 4: Customer
    Read reviews: 3: Customer
  section Purchase
    Checkout: 2: Customer, Bank
invalid:
journey
  section Research
    Compare models, 4, Customer

types.use_for: SysML requirements and the elements satisfying them
rules: Blocks: requirement, functionalRequirement, interfaceRequirement, performanceRequirement, physicalRequirement, designConstraint, element {type, docref}.

Fields only: id, text, risk (low|medium|high), verifymethod (analysis|inspection|test|demonstration); quote id, text, type and docref values that have colons, slashes or hyphens: id: "REQ-001", docref: "docs/mfa-guide.md".
Relations `a - satisfies -> b`: contains, copies, derives, satisfies, verifies, refines, traces; `-->` fails.

types.use_for: C4 model of people and systems (C4Container, C4Component, C4Dynamic, C4Deployment work alike)
rules: Call syntax with commas and double-quoted strings: Person(id, "Label", "Description"); System, SystemDb, System_Ext, Person_Ext.
Boundaries need braces: Enterprise_Boundary(id, "Label") { ... }.
Links only via Rel(from, to, "label", "tech") or BiRel(...); `-->` fails.
types.example:
C4Context
  title Online shop
  Person(customer, "Customer", "Buys products")
  Enterprise_Boundary(b0, "Shop") {
    System(web, "Web store", "Catalogue and checkout")
    SystemDb(db, "Orders DB")
  }
  System_Ext(pay, "Payment provider")
  Rel(customer, web, "Uses", "HTTPS")
  Rel(web, pay, "Charges cards")
invalid:
C4Context
  Person(user, User of the app)

types.use_for: quantities flowing between stages (energy, budget, traffic)
rules: CSV rows `source,target,value`, one per line; no header row, no arrows.
Quote names containing commas: "Gas, oil",Grid,25.
ASCII only: accented letters fail even inside quotes; drop the accents.
types.example:
sankey-beta
Solar,Grid,40
Wind,Grid,35
"Gas, oil",Grid,25
Grid,Homes,60
Grid,Industry,30
Grid,Losses,10

types.use_for: bar and/or line chart
rules: `x-axis [a, b, c]` or `x-axis "Title" 0 --> 100`; series `bar [1, 2]`, `line "Name" [3, 4]` need brackets and plain numbers (no %).
Quote any title, category or name with accents. `xychart-beta horizontal` flips it.
types.example:
xychart-beta
  title "Monthly sales"
  x-axis [Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr]
  y-axis "Revenue (k$)" 0 --> 100
  bar "Sales" [30, 55, 80, 65]
  line "Target" [40, 50, 60, 70]

types.use_for: blocks on a manual column grid (layered system views)
rules: `columns N` sets the grid; `id:2` spans 2 columns; `space` / `space:2` leaves gaps.
Groups are `block:id:span ... end` (no subgraph). Quote labels with spaces: a["Web app"], db[("DB")].
Edges `a --> b` or `a -- "label" --> b`.
types.example:
block-beta
  columns 3
  user["User"] space api["API gateway"]
  block:backend:3
    columns 2
    svc("Orders service") db[("Database")]
  end
  user --> api
  api -- "REST" --> svc
  svc --> db

types.use_for: bit layout of a packet, protocol header or register
rules: Fields `start-end: "Label"`, `bit: "Label"` or `+N: "Label"` (N bits); labels must be quoted.
Ranges start at 0, are contiguous (no gaps/overlaps) and written low-high.
types.example:
packet
  title UDP header
  0-15: "Source port"
  16-31: "Destination port"
  +16: "Length"
  +16: "Checksum"
  64-95: "Data"

types.use_for: kanban board of tasks by status column
rules: Columns `id[Title]`; tasks `id[Task]` indented under their column; ids unique.
Task metadata: @{ assigned: 'ana', ticket: PRJ-12, priority: 'High' } (priority: 'Very High', 'High', 'Low', 'Very Low').
types.example:
kanban
  todo[To do]
    t1[Write spec]@{ assigned: 'ana', priority: 'High' }
    t2[Design API]
  doing[In progress]
    t3[Build login]@{ ticket: PRJ-12 }
  done[Done]
    t4[Set up CI]

types.use_for: cloud/infrastructure services and groups with icons
rules: `group id(icon)[Label]`, `service id(icon)[Label] in group`, `junction id`; icons: cloud, database, disk, internet, server.
Edges name a side at both ends: `a:R --> L:b` (T, B, L, R; `--` = no arrow); `a --> b` fails.
Groups have no body: no braces and no `end`; put each service in its group with `in groupId`. Ids ASCII, labels free text.
types.example:
architecture-beta
  group cloud(cloud)[Public cloud]
  service web(internet)[Web app] in cloud
  service api(server)[API] in cloud
  service db(database)[Database] in cloud
  service files(disk)[Files] in cloud
  web:R --> L:api
  api:R --> L:db
  api:B --> T:files
invalid:
architecture-beta
  service a(server)[API]
  service b(database)[DB]
  a --> b

architecture-beta
  group g(cloud)[Cloud]
    service a(server)[API] in g
  end

types.use_for: radar/spider chart comparing items on several criteria
rules: `axis id["Label"], id2["Label"]` comma-separated; `curve id["Label"]{v1, v2, ...}` with braces, one value per axis in order.
ids ASCII (accents go in the quoted label); scale with `max N` / `min N`.
types.example:
radar-beta
  title Team skills
  axis code["Coding"], test["Testing"], docs["Docs"]
  axis ops["Operations"], ux["UX"]
  curve ana["Ana"]{4, 3, 5, 2, 4}
  curve ben["Ben"]{2, 5, 3, 4, 3}
  max 5
  min 0
invalid:
radar-beta
  axis a, b, c
  curve x[1, 2, 3]

types.use_for: nested rectangles sized by value (budget, disk usage, market share)
rules: Every name double-quoted; leaves `"Name": number`, parents without value; nesting by indentation.
types.example:
treemap-beta
"Budget"
    "Engineering"
        "Salaries": 500
        "Cloud": 120
    "Marketing"
        "Ads": 200

types.use_for: overlapping sets / what groups share
rules: Declare `set Id["Label"]` before use; `union A,B["Label"]` separates set ids with commas.
Ids are ASCII words (accents go in the ["label"]); optional size `:N`; indented `text id["Item"]` adds items.
types.example:
venn-beta
  title "Data science skills"
  set Math["Statistics"]
  set Code["Programming"]
  set Domain["Domain expertise"]
  union Math,Code["Machine learning"]
  union Math,Code,Domain["Data science"]
    text ds1["Python"]
invalid:
venn-beta
  set A
  set B
  union A B

types.use_for: UML use cases: actors, use cases, system boundary
rules: Declare actors `actor Id` or `actor Id("Label")` (undeclared names become use cases); use cases Id("Label") ellipse, Id[Label] box.
`systemBoundary id["Title"] ... end` (no braces). Include/extend: `A ..> : include B`, `A ..> : extend B`; generalize `A --|> B`.
One statement per line, no semicolons; ids ASCII; quote labels with parentheses.
types.example:
usecase-beta
  direction LR
  actor Customer("Online customer")
  systemBoundary shop["Online shop"]
    Browse("Browse catalogue")
    Checkout("Check out")
    Pay("Pay by card")
  end
  Customer --> Browse
  Customer --> Checkout
  Checkout ..> : include Pay
invalid:
usecase-beta
  actor User
  Login
  Auth
  Login ..> Auth : include

types.use_for: process flow in lanes by owner/team (cross-functional flowchart)
rules: Flowchart syntax; each top-level `subgraph id [Lane] ... end` is a lane; optional direction (LR, TB) after the keyword.
Declare each node in one lane only; nested subgraphs are boxes, not lanes. classDef/style work.
types.example:
swimlane-beta LR
  subgraph customer [Customer]
    order[Place order]
    receive([Receive goods])
  end
  subgraph store [Store]
    check{In stock?}
    ship[Ship order]
  end
  order --> check
  check -->|yes| ship --> receive
  check -.->|no| order
invalid:
swimlane-beta
  subgraph A
    x[Step]
  subgraph B
    y[Step]
  end

types.use_for: LLM agent workflows: agents, tasks, tools, decisions, docs
rules: Containers `flow id["Label"] ... end` (not subgraph); nodes `id["Label"]@{ shape: task }`.
Shapes: task, tool, input, decision, refdoc, action or a Mermaid shape name; unknown ones fail.
Only these edges: `-->` sequence, `-.-` reference (no arrowhead), `--x` failure, labels `-- yes -->` or `-->|yes|`. There is no dotted or thick arrow: `-.->` and `==>` fail.

types.use_for: cause-and-effect / fishbone root-cause analysis
rules: First line is the problem; categories below it; causes indented under categories. Plain text, no bullets or arrows.
types.example:
ishikawa-beta
    Late deliveries
    People
        Untrained drivers
    Process
        Manual route planning
    Equipment
        Old trucks
            Frequent breakdowns

types.use_for: Cynefin framework: classify situations by domain
rules: Domain blocks only: complex, complicated, clear, chaotic, confusion (not simple or disorder).
Items are quoted strings, one per line under their domain; unquoted text fails.
Transitions `complex --> complicated : "label"` (label quoted or omitted).
types.example:
cynefin-beta
  title Incident handling
  complex
    "Intermittent outage"
  complicated
    "Slow database queries"
  clear
    "Expired certificate"
  chaotic
    "Data center down"
  confusion
    "Report without details"
  chaotic --> complex : "Stabilized"

types.use_for: Wardley map: value chain by visibility and evolution (strategy)
rules: Coordinates `[visibility, evolution]`, each 0 to 1 (not x, y); `evolve Name 0.8` takes a bare number.
Quote names with accents, a leading digit, '/' or '.': component "Café" [0.5, 0.4] (spaces, hyphens fine).
`anchor` for users; `A -> B` links; decorators (inertia), (build), (buy), (outsource); note "text" [v, e].
types.example:
wardley-beta
  title Tea shop
  anchor Customer [0.95, 0.60]
  component Cup of tea [0.80, 0.55]
  component Kettle [0.45, 0.35] (inertia)
  component "Power grid" [0.15, 0.90] (buy)
  Customer -> Cup of tea
  Cup of tea -> Kettle
  Kettle -> "Power grid"
  evolve Kettle 0.70

types.use_for: file/folder tree or similar hierarchy
rules: Nesting by indentation; trailing / marks a folder; `## text` adds a description.
types.example:
treeView-beta
    my-app/
        src/
            main.ts ## entry point
            utils/
                format.ts
        tests/
        package.json

types.use_for: event modeling: screens, commands, events, read models over time
rules: One frame per line `tf NN type Name`, NN unique; types ui, cmd, evt, rmo (read model), pcr (processor).
Name is one ASCII token (letters, digits, _, . for namespace): no spaces, hyphens or accents.
Links are inferred in order; add one with `->> NN`; `rf` instead of `tf` breaks the inferred link.
types.example:
eventmodeling
  tf 01 ui CartPage
  tf 02 cmd AddItem { sku: string }
  tf 03 evt ItemAdded
  tf 04 rmo CartSummary ->> 03
  tf 05 ui CheckoutPage
  tf 06 cmd PlaceOrder
  tf 07 evt OrderPlaced
invalid:
eventmodeling
  tf 01 ui CartPage
  tf 01 cmd AddItem

types.use_for: railroad diagram of a grammar or command syntax
rules: Rules `name = ctor(...) ;` end with `;`; ctors: sequence, choice, optional, zeroOrMore, oneOrMore, terminal("x"), nonterminal("x").
Strings quoted, no trailing commas, ASCII rule names. EBNF/ABNF/PEG text needs railroad-ebnf-beta / -abnf-beta / -peg-beta.
